paragraph: No stage is set. No figure for Angola's gender gap in internet use has been found for 2023 or later. The latest held is 9.82 per cent, for 2014. The gap is men's rate of internet use less women's, as a share of men's. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a figure for 2023 or later of 30 per cent or less, from ITU's series or a national household survey.

In 2024, [the gender gap in internet use in Botswana was -1.93 per cent](<https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/dataportal>), by the ITU's internet use series by sex. The gap is men's rate of internet use less women's, as a share of men's, so below zero women's use is the higher. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The series gives no figure for the years just before, so no source found says whether the gap is rising or falling. It measures the difference between women and men, not how many use the internet.

In 2024, [the gender gap in internet use in Cote d'Ivoire was 13.9 per cent](<https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/dataportal>), by the internet use series by sex of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). The same series [gives 21.7 per cent in 2022 and 23.9 per cent in 2023](<https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/dataportal>). No other change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 10 per cent or less has been found. Operating would need a gap of 10 per cent or less.

In August and September 2024, [Afrobarometer found 84.4 per cent of men and 81.4 per cent of women use the internet at least a few times a month](<https://www.afrobarometer.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Summary-of-results-Cabo-Verde-Afrobarometer-R10-Eng-19march25.pdf>). That is a gap of 3.6 per cent. ITU's series gave 3.0 per cent for 2019. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 2 per cent or less has been found. Mature would need a gap of 2 per cent or less.
